competences: The learner identifies sourced facts about human rights.
The learner explains information relating to Rights of a citizen and the Uganda Human Rights Commission.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads and spells: human rights, rights, commission, citizen.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to state facts about human rights.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer original sourced questions on Rights of a citizen and the Uganda Human Rights Commission.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied related ideas about Uganda and its population or government. They use this knowledge in studying human rights.
materials: P5 SST notes about Rights of a citizen and the Uganda Human Rights Commission
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher asks learners to recall earlier Social Studies work and introduces human rights. They ask the original question "Give any two examples of human rights" and note the learners' responses before teaching the content.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous work, answer the opening question and explain what they already know about Uganda and its people.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about human rights
steps.content: By forming organisations that ensure the protection of human rights. Note: The Uganda Human Rights Commission (UHRC) was set up in Uganda to ensure protection of human rights By reporting the cases of human rights abuse. By helping the police in arresting people who violate human rights. To investigate the violation of human rights. To promote human rights. Observance of human rights. Briefly describe the term human rights. Every grown up has the right to marry. Human rights violation This is the denial of the basic human freedoms people are entitled to. Forms of human rights abuse Death penalty. How the government can protect people against the human rights violation.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Meaning and key facts about human rights", starting with "By forming organisations that ensure the protection of human rights. Note: The Uganda Human Rights Commission (UHRC) was set up in Uganda to ensure protection of human rights;". They explain the information, clarify the meanings and check learners' understanding through questioning.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source notes, explain the main points, answer their teacher's questions and copy the factual information into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and related facts about human rights
steps.content: By enforcing laws against human rights abuse. To educate the citizens about their rights. By respecting other people’s rights. By sensitising other people about their rights. The Uganda Human Rights Commission (UHRC) A citizen is a person who enjoys full civil democratic and human rights in a country. Or Promoting human rights Uganda human rights commission The Uganda Human rights commission (government owned)
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Features and related facts about human rights", starting with "By enforcing laws against human rights abuse.; To educate the citizens about their rights.". They explain the information, clarify the meanings and check learners' understanding through questioning.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source notes, explain the main points, answer their teacher's questions and copy the factual information into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Further details about human rights
steps.content: There was detention (imprisonment) without trial. There was massive killing of people during Amin’s regime Women were raped Political opponents were kidnapped and never to be seen again Amin declared an economic war which brought about scarcity of essential goods like soap, salt, sugar etc. Example of people who were killed during Amin’s regime Archibishop Janan Luwum Erinayo Oryema in 1977 Dumping grounds for bodies of some of the murdered people during Amin’s regime. Owen falls dam. Violation of human rights by some departments like police etc
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Further details about human rights", starting with "There was detention (imprisonment) without trial.; There was massive killing of people during Amin’s regime". They explain the information, clarify the meanings and check learners' understanding through questioning.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source notes, explain the main points, answer their teacher's questions and copy the factual information into their books.

steps.content: Give any two examples of human rights | Define human rights abuse. | Write down two ways human rights have been abused today. | Give two internal organizations that help to protect human rights. | Mention two internal organizations that protect human rights.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher presents the exact sourced questions, beginning with "Give any two examples of human rights" and "Define human rights abuse.". They supervise the written responses, check the answers against the lesson notes and correct errors.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the questions in their books, compare their work with the factual notes and correct wrong or incomplete answers.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the important facts about human rights and evaluates learning using "Give any two examples of human rights" and "Define human rights abuse.". They give guidance on the remaining original exercise for home revision.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer final oral questions, mention one important fact and make corrections in their notebooks before the lesson ends.

assessment: Use the original questions "Give any two examples of human rights" and "Define human rights abuse." and other exercises to test understanding. Mark answers and assist pupils to correct them using the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining original sourced exercise questions, especially "Which body protects human rights in Uganda?"
